subject: Re: SDLC evidence request — CI approvals, short-lived secrets, and merge attestations
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@avalon-assessors.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 21 Mar 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SDLC artifacts request — CI approvals, secrets lifecycle, and merge attestations

Hi Lauren,

Following our intake call this morning I put together a concise list of artifacts Avalon needs to complete the Secure SDLC assessment for Avalon Bank's vendor review. Please send the items below or tell me if any will take longer than three business days.

1) Evidence of PR gating and merge approvals for the last 90 days for main and release branches (signed approver metadata preferred).
2) CI job policy snapshots showing required reviewers / job approvals (e.g., merge gating jobs that require CI pass + approver).
3) Example CI job logs that show ephemeral secret injection (short-lived Vault tokens) with timestamps.
4) Keystore/KMS rotation evidence and the current policy for secret TTLs used by CI runners.
5) A short narrative on how emergency change procedures are handled (who can bypass gating, escalation path, and retroactive attestations).

If you have a manifest file or checklist for what you'll provide, that helps our tracker. Also flag any redactions in advance.

Thanks,
Elena Rossi
Senior Assessor — Avalon Assessors
elena.rossi@avalon-assessors.com

Attachment: intake-checklist-avalon-20290321.pdf (application/pdf)
From: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@avalon-assessors.com>
Cc: jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 21 Mar 2029 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SDLC artifacts request — CI approvals, secrets lifecycle, and merge attestations

Elena — thanks for the clear list. We're on it. Quick plan and what we can deliver within 3 business days: 

- Immediate (by EOD 3/22): branch protection snapshot (includes required status checks and required reviewers), brief narrative of emergency bypass flow, and the Vault rotation snapshot.
- By 3/25: signed merge attestations for the last 90 days tied to PR numbers, CSV roster of CI job approvals, and 3 anonymized CI job logs showing ephemeral token injection.
- If you need longer retention artifacts (audit log exports beyond 90 days) let us know and we can request them from infra.

We'll attach a manifest to the deliverable and call out any redactions (usernames replaced with role tags). Jordan will gather the CI logs and Karthik will pull Vault/KMS evidence.

Lauren Bishop
Director, Trust & Security
Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: branch-protection-snapshot-20290321.json (application/json), vault-rotation-snapshot-20290320.txt (text/plain)
From: jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com
To: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 22 Mar 2029 14:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SDLC artifacts request — CI approvals, secrets lifecycle, and merge attestations

Rapid progress update and clarifications for Elena (copied through lauren once we compile):

- CI job logs: I'll redact personally identifiable usernames and provide three representative runs: one normal PR merge, one canary deploy, and one emergency hotfix merge where the change-left review was logged post-merge (with rollback steps). Logs will show ephemeral Vault tokens injected via GitHub Actions OIDC to Vault broker, TTLs (600s), and a short-lived role binding.
- Merge attestations: we have a signed attestation workflow that stamps merge metadata with reviewer ID + timestamp via our internal webhook. I can export the last 90 days and produce a PDF bundle of signed attestations.
- CI approvals roster: CSV will contain PR#, required approver role, approver-email (redacted to role@redwoodinference.com), job-name, and approval-timestamp.

Note: Emergency bypass is rare and requires a two-person exec override plus a post-mortem and retroactive attestation. We'll include one anonymized example.

I'll upload the compiled bundle to the shared drive link and ping you both once complete.

- Jordan

Attachments referenced: ci-job-logs-sample-20290320.zip (zip), merge-attestations-20290325.pdf (pdf)
From: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@avalon-assessors.com>
Cc: jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 25 Mar 2029 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SDLC artifacts request — CI approvals, secrets lifecycle, and merge attestations

Hi Elena — bundle uploaded to the Drive link below and copies attached to this message. Manifest included. Summary of what's provided: 

- branch-protection-snapshot-20290321.json: GitHub org and repo protection rules (required status checks, required reviewers, enforce-merge-queue).
- ci-approval-roster-20290325.csv: per-PR approval roster (roles redacted).
- merge-attestations-20290325.pdf: exported attestations with webhook signatures; sensitive fields redacted and replaced with role tags.
- ci-job-logs-sample-20290320.zip: three representative CI runs; logs show OIDC->Vault exchange, ephemeral token TTLs, and job approval gates.
- vault-rotation-snapshot-20290320.txt: Key rotation registry and last rotation times for CI roles.

Emergency change procedure: two-person executive override required (exec1 + security lead) with mandatory post-merge attestation. We included one anonymized emergency case with timeline and rollback steps.

If you want full raw audit logs (unredacted) we will process a formal proof request and provide a separate secure transfer (SFTP or secure Share). Let me know if the redactions are acceptable for your review or if you need user-level detail for any PR.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call to walk through the artifacts if helpful.

Lauren Bishop
Director, Trust & Security
Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: branch-protection-snapshot-20290321.json, ci-approval-roster-20290325.csv, merge-attestations-20290325.pdf, ci-job-logs-sample-20290320.zip, vault-rotation-snapshot-20290320.txt
